items.prompt: What is the story mostly about?

options.text: Dewi finds a way to keep the fruit dry in the rain.
Grandma buys a new umbrella for the stall.
options.why: Grandma does not buy an umbrella. The flower seller has an old one.

options.text: The fish seller sells all his fish.
options.why: The fish seller is only mentioned once.

options.text: Dewi learns to count the mangoes.
options.why: Counting mangoes is not part of the story.

hints: Think about the problem in the story.
What did Dewi do to fix the problem?
Read the middle part again, where Dewi cries out to Grandma.
items.explanation: The problem is the rain, and Dewi solves it by covering the fruit with banana leaves. That is what most of the story is about.

items.prompt: Which title would also fit this story?

options.why: The blue sheet is only a small detail.
A lady buys six mangoes, but the story is not about that.

options.text: A sunny day at the market
options.why: Most of the story is about rain, not sunshine.

hints: A good title tells you what the whole story is about.
What was the problem, and who solved it?
Think about what Grandma says to Dewi at the end.
items.explanation: The whole story is about Dewi's idea to cover the fruit with banana leaves, so Dewi's clever idea fits best.

items.prompt: What do adult green sea turtles mostly eat?

options.why: Young turtles eat these. The question asks about adults.
The text does not say that adults eat fish.
Turtles do not eat sand.

hints: Find the part with the subheading What do they eat?
That part talks about young turtles and about adults.
Read the sentence that starts with Adults.
items.explanation: The text says adults mostly eat seagrass and seaweed. Jellyfish and crabs are eaten by young turtles.

items.prompt: Why is it called a green sea turtle?

options.why: It does eat seaweed, but that is not where the name comes from.

options.text: The fat under its shell is green.

options.why: The text says the shell is mostly brown or olive.
The text does not say this.

hints: Find the part called What do they look like?
Look for the words named after.
Read the whole sentence after named after, and the sentence after it.
items.explanation: The text says the turtle is named after the green colour of the fat under its shell. The shell itself is mostly brown or olive.

items.prompt:
Read this new sentence.
Some people guard the nests at night so that nobody takes the eggs.
Which section should it go in?

options.why: That section describes the turtle's body.
That section is about food.
The sentence mentions eggs, but it is about how people help turtles.

hints: Read the new sentence. Who is doing something in it?
Each section has its own main idea.
Read the first sentence of each section to remind yourself what it is about.
items.explanation: The new sentence is about people protecting the turtles' nests. That matches the main idea of the Helping turtles section.

items.prompt: What did the poet use to make the kite?

options.why: The poem does not mention plastic or wire.
Leaves are not part of the kite.
The poem says paper, not cloth.

hints: Read the first verse of the poem.
Look for the things the kite was made from.
The first two lines tell you.
items.explanation: The first verse says the kite was made of red paper, bamboo sticks and cotton thread.

items.prompt: Which sentence best sums up the poem?

options.text: The poet waits for the wind, flies the kite high and happily brings it home.
The poet's kite breaks in a storm.
options.why: There is no storm, and the kite comes home safely.

options.text: A mynah bird steals the poet's kite.
options.why: The mynah bird only circles once and flies away.

options.text: The poet buys a kite at the market.
options.why: The poet made the kite.

hints: Think about the beginning, the middle and the end of the poem.
What happens to the kite first, then later, then at the end?
Check each answer against the last verse.
items.explanation: At first there is no wind. Then a breeze lifts the kite high, and in the evening the poet winds it in and thanks the wind.

items.prompt: Where did Lucy find the library book?

options.why: Mrs Lim says to keep the book in the bag next time, so it was not there.
The book was in the classroom.
Amir looked under the desks, but it was not there.

options.text: under a pile of painting paper

hints: Think about where Amir last used the book.
Lucy remembers what the class did after quiet reading time.
Read what Lucy does when she hurries to the window.
items.explanation: Lucy lifted a pile of painting paper on the table by the window and found the yellow book underneath.

items.prompt: Why did Bima write this letter?

options.text: to ask Grandad for a new book
options.why: Bima already has the book. He is saying thank you.

options.text: to say thank you and tell Grandad about his trip
to give Grandad instructions for picking tea
options.why: Bima tells how tea is picked, but that is not why he wrote.

options.text: to invite Grandad to his birthday party
options.why: The birthday has already happened.

hints: Read the first paragraph, then the middle of the letter.
What two things does Bima tell Grandad?
Think about the first line and what most of the letter is about.
items.explanation: Bima thanks Grandad for the drawing book, and most of the letter tells him about the class trip to the tea garden.

items.prompt: What do you have after step 4?

options.why: You make a diamond in step 5.
The boat only pops open in step 8.
There is no cup in these instructions.

hints: Find step 4 in the list.
Read to the very end of step 4.
Look for the words Now you have.
items.explanation: Step 4 ends with Now you have a paper hat! The diamond comes in step 5.

items.prompt: What is the main idea of this report?

options.text: Pandas eat bamboo for much of the day.
options.why: This is one fun fact at the end, not the main idea.

options.text: The angklung is a musical instrument.
options.why: This is one detail in one section.

options.text: Bamboo is a kind of tree.
options.why: The report says bamboo looks like a tree but is really a grass.

options.text: Bamboo is a fast-growing grass that people use in many ways.

hints: The main idea is what the whole text is about, not one small detail.
Look at the title and all the subheadings.
Which answer fits every section of the report?
items.explanation: The report explains that bamboo is a grass, that it grows fast and that people use it in many ways. That idea links all the sections.

items.prompt: What is a bamboo stem called? Write one word.
hints: Find the section called Fast growers.
Look for the words A bamboo stem is called.
The word you need comes straight after called.
items.explanation: The report says a bamboo stem is called a culm.

items.prompt: Listen to the passage. What is it mostly about?
hints: Listen for what happens first, next and last.
The same animal is in every sentence.
Think about the whole passage, not just one sentence.
items.explanation: The speaker described how frog eggs become tadpoles and then frogs. The passage is mostly about how a frog grows.
items.listenText: Frogs begin life as eggs in water. The eggs become tadpoles. The tadpoles grow legs and become frogs.

items.prompt: Many animals sleep through the cold winter. Bears find a cave and sleep for months. Some frogs bury themselves in mud. This long sleep is called hibernation.
hints: Read the first sentence. It often gives the main idea.
The last sentence has a special word.
The word starts with the letter h.
items.explanation: The main idea is that some animals sleep through winter. The long sleep is called hibernation.
